clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A hospitalized client will ambulate to the bathroom. Which footwear best supports fall prevention?

options.A: Use well-fitting footwear with a firm shape, low stable heel, and nonslip tread, or appropriate gripper socks when safe shoes cannot be worn.
options.B: Use loose socks with a smooth sole so the client's feet can slide easily during turns and short-distance walking to the bathroom.
options.C: Allow the client to walk barefoot on a dry polished floor because direct foot contact provides better balance than fitted footwear.
options.D: Use loose backless slippers with a raised heel and minimal tread because they can be removed quickly if the client becomes unsteady.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current AHRQ-hosted fall-prevention guidance recommends footwear that fits well, has a firm shape, a low even heel, and tread on the sole; gripper socks are recommended when safe shoes or slippers cannot be worn. AHRQ-described inpatient fall-prevention practice also includes use of nonskid gripper socks as part of hospital fall precautions. Therefore secure, nonslip footwear is preferable during ambulation. B is incorrect because loose smooth-soled socks increase slipping risk. C is incorrect because barefoot ambulation on a polished surface does not provide the supported fall-prevention features. D is incorrect because loose backless, raised-heel footwear is less stable and lacks the recommended secure fit and tread.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Select secure, well-fitting footwear with nonslip tread for ambulation and use appropriate gripper socks when safe shoes cannot be worn.

audit_findings_append.finding: One clearly best fall-prevention footwear choice with balanced distractors and no length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches AHRQ-supported secure fit, tread, low stable heel, and gripper-sock alternatives.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Loose smooth-soled socks can increase slipping risk.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Barefoot walking on a polished floor lacks supported nonslip footwear protection.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Loose backless raised-heel slippers do not provide the recommended secure fit and tread.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely contains the supported footwear characteristics; B-D introduce unstable or slippery footwear conditions.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel footwear choices of comparable length and specificity; the prior uniquely-long correct response was removed.
